decisions.reason: As a large, R&D-active machinery firm in a growing market, it is likely to retain this core-adjacent coolant pressure booster system because it fits existing capabilities and there is no sign its early results fall below aspiration levels.

The coolant cleaning centrifuge builds directly on the firm's established coolant-management business, so with organisational slack and no evidence of underperformance management would likely keep it on the market.

Although coolant nozzles may be easier to substitute and could be pruned if they disappoint, their close fit with the existing offer and the firm's broad portfolio make continued market presence more likely than withdrawal.

The scraper belt chip conveyor is near the core business and supports the firm's automation and material-flow strategy, but as a close rather than fully established extension it faces a somewhat higher review risk if sales do not quickly meet aspirations.

This magnetic belt chip conveyor aligns well with the firm's established conveying solutions, and a large incumbent with engineering slack would usually keep such a related product unless clear shortfalls emerged.

The hinged belt chip conveyor is a sensible adjacent addition to the portfolio, and absent evidence of poor results the firm would likely keep it, though overlap with other conveyor variants raises the chance of later rationalisation somewhat.
